stories.title: Burnham cancels engagements after death of father
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cancelled official engagements on Monday and Tuesday following the death of his father Roy, who had Alzheimer's disease. Opposition leaders from all major parties expressed condolences.

stories.title: UK's Burnham welcomes AI bosses' focus on risks of emerging technology
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has welcomed the focus by AI industry leaders on the risks their technology could pose to humanity. A Downing Street spokesperson confirmed Burnham's position amid growing debate on AI safety.

stories.title: Burnham rejects Celtic nations' claims UK may break up
stories.summary: No 10 rejected claims by SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin that the UK is approaching a constitutional breaking point, even as the three nationalist parties signed a joint pact in Cardiff calling for independence referendums.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Burnham: UK an 'outsourced state with little accountability'
stories.summary: Before becoming PM, Burnham reportedly told Labour MPs that Britain had become an 'outsourced state with little accountability' and that he wanted to bring services back in-house. This signals a potential shift in procurement philosophy away from heavy private sector outsourcing.

stories.title: 🤖 OpenAI urges UK lawmakers to rein in AI amid growing safety fears
stories.summary: OpenAI has urged UK lawmakers to take action on AI regulation, while more than 70 MPs and peers have separately urged PM Burnham to back a ban on artificial superintelligence (ASI). Burnham has welcomed the growing focus on AI safety risks from industry leaders.

stories.title: 🤖 GOV.UK One Login introduces biometric passkeys
stories.summary: The government's central digital identity platform GOV.UK One Login has launched biometric passkey support, marking a significant step forward in secure digital identity verification for public services.

stories.title: 🏢 Whitehall pensions crisis: 'Capita performance remains unacceptable', minister says
stories.summary: A minister has stated that Capita's performance on the Whitehall pensions administration contract 'remains unacceptable', intensifying scrutiny of the government's relationship with the outsourcing giant amid ongoing service failures.

stories.title: 🤖 Digital ID: Ministers cite OBR cost figures that predecessors rejected
stories.summary: Government ministers are using Office for Budget Responsibility cost estimates for the Digital ID programme that their predecessors had rejected as inaccurate, raising questions about the transparency and consistency of the scheme's business case.

stories.title: 🤖 L-plates and safety warnings for AI in healthcare
stories.summary: The MHRA has published a report welcoming AI in healthcare but calling for strict guardrails and safety protocols. The report recommends treating AI deployments in NHS settings like learner drivers - with oversight and caution.

stories.title: 💰 Britain, Burnham and tax: the fiscal walls close in
stories.summary: The Financial Times reports that PM Burnham and Chancellor sought to project optimism on taking office in July, but are now facing mounting fiscal pressures. The government's tax and spending stance is under increasing scrutiny.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Reform's £72m donations may not be legal under Representation of the People Bill
stories.summary: The Representation of the People Bill, currently progressing through Parliament, contains provisions that would cap political party donations. Farage has hinted that Reform's record £72m donations from two crypto billionaires may not comply when the bill becomes law.

stories.title: More than 100 peers call on colleagues to 'complete the task' on assisted dying bill
stories.summary: Over 100 House of Lords peers have signed a letter urging their colleagues to support the assisted dying legislation, which MPs voted on in September. The bill now moves back to the Lords for consideration.

stories.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' policy raises concerns for UK business
stories.summary: PM Burnham has warned that UK businesses will face 'significant problems' from the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act, designed to protect against unfair competition. Parliament is expected to debate the UK's response to this European policy shift.

stories.title: Ministers face backlash from hospitality industry over 'tourist tax' plans
stories.summary: Labour ministers are facing pushback from the hospitality sector over proposed 'tourist tax' policies. Industry leaders warn the plans could damage UK tourism and hospitality businesses already under financial pressure.

stories.title: TUC chief warns 'super-rich' threaten democracy as unions intervene on party funding
stories.summary: The TUC General Secretary has warned that 'super-rich' donors are corrupting British politics following Reform's £72m windfall, with unions set to intervene in debates around political funding reforms. Labour is facing pressure to act on donation caps.

stories.title: Burnham to abstain from assisted dying vote
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham is expected to abstain from the vote on the assisted dying legislation, reflecting his personal position on the contentious issue while allowing a free vote among Labour MPs.

stories.title: Badenoch offers condolences to PM Burnham on father's death
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch offered heartfelt condolences to PM Burnham following the death of his father Roy, saying 'losing your father is a profoundly painful experience. A part of your life that has always been there is suddenly gone.'

stories.title: Tories appoint shadow minister for war readiness amid wider reshuffle
stories.summary: The Conservative Party has appointed a new shadow minister for war readiness as part of a broader reshuffle of Badenoch's top team. The appointment signals the party's intent to challenge the government on defence preparedness.

stories.title: Conservatives oppose retrospective donations cap as 'extraordinary measure'
stories.summary: A shadow Cabinet Office minister has called the government's plans to impose a retrospective cap on political donations 'an extraordinary measure', opposing attempts to apply new election funding rules to Reform's £72m already received.

stories.title: Ed Davey sends condolences to PM Burnham on father's death
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey expressed his sympathies to Prime Minister Burnham following the death of his father Roy, saying 'my heart goes out to the prime minister on the loss of his dad. From our conversations he sounded like a wonderful man.'

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Farage says £72m Reform donations 'compliant with the law today'
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage defended two £36m donations from crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, insisting they are '100% compliant with the law today' while acknowledging they may not comply with the proposed Representation of the People Bill.

stories.title: Record 69% of Brits now hold unfavourable view of Farage
stories.summary: A YouGov poll found a record 69% of British voters hold an unfavourable view of Nigel Farage — the highest level recorded in a decade of tracking. Just 24% view him favourably. The surge in negative opinion follows the controversy over Reform's £72m donations.

stories.title: Reform threatens to ban unions from donating to parties if Labour acts retrospectively
stories.summary: Nigel Farage has said Reform UK could push to ban trade unions from donating to political parties if Labour seeks to change election funding laws retrospectively to target Reform's £72m donation haul.

stories.title: SNP, Plaid Cymru and Sinn Féin sign pact to make Burnham 'the last UK Prime Minister'
stories.summary: The leaders of the three nationalist parties signed a joint agreement in Cardiff to coordinate their independence ambitions, following US President Trump's surprise backing for a united Ireland. Scotland's John Swinney predicted Burnham would be the 'last PM of the UK'.

stories.title: Westminster's time is coming to an end, say first ministers of UK's Celtic nations
stories.summary: The first ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland jointly declared that Westminster's era of dominance is ending, as all three devolved administrations are now led by nationalists for the first time. They called for independence referendums and greater devolution.

stories.title: Analysis: Swinney's summit won't break up UK — but Burnham should worry
stories.summary: Despite the dramatic rhetoric, analysts suggest Swinney's nationalist summit is unlikely to immediately threaten UK unity. However, the coordinated challenge from all three devolved nations creates a significant political headache for PM Burnham.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Burnham rejects Celtic nations' calls for constitutional change ahead of devolution discussions
stories.summary: The Cabinet Office and No 10 have rejected claims from SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin that the UK is approaching a constitutional breaking point, while indicating that the government remains committed to its own devolution agenda.

stories.title: MHCLG forms dedicated content improvement team
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government has formed a new dedicated content improvement team aimed at improving operational efficiency and digital accessibility across its public-facing services.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Polls: Farage at record unpopularity, Burnham steady at 46% favourable
stories.summary: A YouGov poll shows PM Burnham remains at 46% favourable while his unfavourable rating has risen 6 points to 39% in the last month. By contrast, Farage has hit a record 69% unfavourable rating following Reform's £72m donations controversy.

stories.title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises
stories.summary: Election officials have issued guidance urging campaigners to respect their political rivals as reports of abuse targeting candidates during local elections have increased. The Electoral Commission is considering further action.

stories.title: Lords begin debating Representation of the People Bill on donations cap
stories.summary: The House of Lords has started debating the Representation of the People Bill, which includes provisions to cap political donations and tighten overseas funding rules. Reform's £72m donations have put the bill under intense scrutiny.

stories.title: More than 100 peers call on Lords to 'complete the task' on assisted dying
stories.summary: Over 100 peers have signed a letter calling on the House of Lords to support the assisted dying bill and 'complete the task' of legislating on end-of-life care. PM Burnham is expected to abstain from the vote.

stories.title: Lords to debate civil service impartiality on 17 September
stories.summary: The House of Lords is scheduled to hold a short debate on civil service impartiality on 17 September 2026, amid ongoing discussions about the balance between political direction and civil service independence under the new Burnham administration.
